announcements.title: Codex 客户端登录状态检测与凭据刷新说明
announcements.summary: 官方 Codex 客户端最新版增加了新的登录状态检测，部分账号可能在使用一段时间后或者对话后被跳转到登录页面。经过持续排查和大量测试，Cockpit Tools 最新版已调整客户端监测、切号和凭据刷新流程，并与官方最新 OAuth 授权参数保持一致。
announcements.content:
官方 Codex 客户端最新版更新后，增加了一些新的登录状态检测。当客户端请求远端接口并收到特定结果时，部分账号可能在使用一段时间后或者对话后被跳转到登录页面。

最近我们一直在研究这个问题，在不同账号、不同系统和多种使用场景上投入了大量时间和精力，进行了大量测试。期间也连续调整过好几个版本，根据当时的测试结果尝试了多套我们认为可行的认证和切号规则。但随着测试样本增加，最终仍没有找到一个适用于所有账号和环境的固定规律。

同一组登录凭证在不同环境下也可能出现完全不同的结果。例如，同一个账号在我的 macOS 电脑上会退出登录，导入 Windows 后却可能正常使用、不再跳转登录页面。这也说明问题并不能仅通过某一个 Token 的本地状态或一条固定规则准确判断。

另外，Cockpit Tools 最新版本的 OAuth 授权请求已与官方最新桌面客户端的内层授权流程保持一致，使用相同的官方授权端点和主要参数，包括 `client_id`、授权 scope、PKCE、`id_token_add_organizations=true`、`codex_cli_simplified_flow=true` 及 `originator=Codex Desktop`。官方使用的 `https://chatgpt.com/codex/desktop-auth` 属于桌面前端的外层包装，内层仍然是 `https://auth.openai.com/oauth/authorize`；Cockpit 直接使用同一内层 OAuth 协议完成授权。

目前 Cockpit Tools 最新版本已经采用以下逻辑：

1. 监听客户端实际登录状态
Cockpit 会监听 Codex 客户端是否真正跳转到登录页面。确认跳转后，只会给对应账号添加提示标记，由用户自行决定是否重新授权，不会强制阻止切号。

2. 切号不再受本地 Token 到期信息强制限制
切号不会再仅因为本地 id_token 等 Token 的过期时间而被拦截。

3. 启动预览支持手动刷新登录凭证
启动预览中增加了强制刷新功能，可以使用当前 refresh_token 获取新的登录凭证，同时检查该 refresh_token 是否仍然有效。刷新失败时，可以选择重新检测或重新授权。

目前通过大量测试能够得到的阶段性结论是：refresh_token 失效不一定会直接导致客户端退出登录；但已经跳转到登录页面的账号，其 refresh_token 基本都已经失效。大部分账号在重新授权并获取新的登录信息后，可以恢复正常使用。

不同系统、客户端版本和账号状态之间仍可能存在差异，因此目前无法承诺某一种规则能够覆盖所有情况。如果你发现了新的触发条件、账号表现或更可靠的处理方式，欢迎通过 GitHub 提交 Issue 或 Pull Request，帮助我们继续完善判断和处理方案。

en.title: Codex client sign-in observation and credential refresh
en.summary: The latest official Codex client introduced new sign-in checks. Some accounts may be redirected to sign-in after being used for a while or after a conversation. Following extensive investigation and testing, the latest Cockpit Tools release updates client observation, switching, and credential refresh behavior while matching the latest official OAuth authorization parameters.
en.content:
The latest official Codex client introduced additional sign-in state checks. When the client receives certain results from remote requests, some accounts may be redirected to the sign-in page after being used for a while or after a conversation.

We have spent substantial time and effort investigating this issue across different accounts, operating systems, and usage scenarios, with extensive testing. Across several releases, we adjusted authentication and switching rules based on what the available results suggested at the time. As the test sample grew, however, we still could not identify one fixed trigger that applies to every account and environment.

The same credentials can behave completely differently across environments. For example, the same account may sign out on my macOS computer while continuing to work normally after being imported on Windows. This also shows that the outcome cannot be determined reliably from one local Token state or a single fixed rule.

In addition, the latest Cockpit Tools version uses the same inner OAuth authorization flow as the latest official desktop client, including the official authorization endpoint and main parameters such as `client_id`, authorization scopes, PKCE, `id_token_add_organizations=true`, `codex_cli_simplified_flow=true`, and `originator=Codex Desktop`. The official `https://chatgpt.com/codex/desktop-auth` URL is an outer wrapper used by the desktop front end; its inner authorization request still targets `https://auth.openai.com/oauth/authorize`. Cockpit uses that same inner OAuth protocol directly.

The latest Cockpit Tools version now uses the following logic:

1. Observe the client's actual sign-in state
Cockpit observes whether the Codex client actually redirects to the sign-in page. If confirmed, it adds a notice to the matching account and lets you decide whether to reauthorize. It does not forcibly block account switching.

2. Do not block switching solely because of local Token expiration
Account switching is no longer blocked only because a local id_token or another Token is shown as expired.

3. Manually refresh credentials from launch preview
Launch preview can use the current refresh_token to obtain new credentials and check whether that refresh_token is still valid. If refresh fails, you can retry or reauthorize.

Our findings from extensive testing so far are: an invalid refresh_token does not always cause the client to sign out, but accounts that have redirected to sign-in generally also have an invalid refresh_token. Most affected accounts return to normal after reauthorization obtains new credentials.

Behavior can still vary by operating system, client version, and account state, so no single rule can currently be guaranteed to cover every case. If you discover a reproducible trigger or a more reliable approach, please submit a GitHub Issue or Pull Request to help us continue improving the detection and recovery flow.

announcements.title: Windows 用户切号跳转登录页问题说明
announcements.summary: 仅使用官方 ChatGPT 客户端也可能遇到切号后跳转登录页的问题。目前 Windows 更新到 ChatGPT 26.825 或更高版本后基本可以恢复。
announcements.content:
近期发现，仅使用官方 ChatGPT 客户端也可能在切换账号后跳转到登录页面，并非只有使用第三方工具才会出现。

目前测试显示，Windows 用户将 ChatGPT 更新到 26.825 或更高版本后，登录跳转问题基本可以恢复。遇到类似问题的用户，建议及时更新官方客户端后再测试。macOS 目前仍可能出现类似问题。

en.title: Windows users: sign-in redirect after account switching
en.summary: The official ChatGPT client can also redirect to sign-in after switching accounts. On Windows, updating to ChatGPT 26.825 or later has generally restored normal behavior in current testing.
en.content:
We found that the official ChatGPT client can redirect to the sign-in page after switching accounts even when no third-party tool is used.

Current testing shows that Windows users generally recover normal behavior after updating ChatGPT to 26.825 or later. If you encounter this issue, update the official client and test again. Similar behavior may still occur on macOS.
